# Tool reference: SimCity 4 server (simcity4)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's tools/list; do not edit by hand -->

108 tools. Every tool takes JSON arguments as described and returns compact JSON text, except `guide` (markdown). Failures are MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) whose text is JSON `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}`.

Kinds map to the MCP tool annotations each tool carries:

| kind | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| read | True | False | True | reads the game, changes nothing |
| observe | True | False | False | reads; has a 'since last call' cursor |
| set | False | False | True | sets a value (idempotent) |
| act | False | False | False | acts in the game |
| destructive | False | True | False | can discard or destroy something (unsaved city, a file, the game process) |

All tools have openWorldHint false (they act on the local game only).

| [`setup_check`](#setup_check) | read | What SiMCP needs on this machine, checked without starting the game: Windows, Python, the game's build, the SiMCP DLLs, SiMCP's home folder, your plugins (mirrored read-only) and NAM. |

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization:

> Tools for playing SimCity 4 Deluxe (1.1.641) through the game's own code. Start with guide(), then game_launch(). Coordinates are city cells; regions are grids of city tiles. Every result is JSON; failures are tool errors with {error, hint}.

## guide

*read*

How to use this server: the guide for agents, by topic.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string | `'start'` | "start" (overview and first steps), "all" (the whole guide) or a section name such as "regions". |

## game_launch

*act*

Start SimCity 4 (or attach to the instance SiMCP started earlier) and connect to it. The game runs without administrator rights and with SiMCP's own user folder (its own Regions and settings; the player's plugins are mirrored, so the simulation is the same), and opens on the region view. Returns the game status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `windowed` | boolean | `true` | run in a window (true) or full screen. |
| `width` | integer | `1024` | window / screen width in pixels (screen recipes are measured at 1024x768). |
| `height` | integer | `768` | window / screen height in pixels. |
| `intro` | boolean | `false` | play the intro movie. |
| `timeout_s` | integer | `120` | seconds to wait for the game to finish starting. |

## game_status

*read*

Whether SimCity 4 is running and controllable, and what it shows (region view or a city).

No parameters.

## list_regions

*read*

The regions in SiMCP's user folder with their city tiles (grid position, size small / medium / large) and each tile's saved city (name, mayor, established or not, populations). Reads files: works without the game.

No parameters.

## saved_city

*read*

A saved city read from its file, without the game: tile, size, populations, mayor rating, difficulty, names; with terrain=true also the saved altitudes at every cell corner.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's name. |
| `city` | string | required | the city's name. |
| `terrain` | boolean | `false` | include the altitude grid (rows of cells+1 values, metres). |

## city_thumbnail

*observe*

The picture the region view shows for a saved city (the game renders it on every save), read from the file.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's name. |
| `city` | string | required | the city's name. |
| `view` | string | `'satellite'` | satellite or transport. |

## open_tile

*act*

Open a city tile of the loaded region by its grid square (the tile's north-west corner, as list_regions gives it), as the region view's Play button does: a saved city loads; an empty tile opens as a new city in god mode (shape the land, then found_city).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | the tile's grid column. |
| `z` | integer | required | the tile's grid row. |

## new_region

*act*

Create a new region in SiMCP's user folder, as the region view's Create New Region does (the game picks a random layout of city tiles; new tiles start flat), and open it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the region's name (letters, digits, spaces, - ' _). |
| `water` | boolean | `false` | start the tiles low (the "Water" terrain choice) instead of plains. |

## backup_region

*act*

Copy a region of SiMCP's user folder (its settings and every city file) into SiMCP's backups folder.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name (list_regions). |

## remove_city

*destructive*

Take a city out of a region: its file is moved into SiMCP's backups (not deleted), and the tile is a new, unfounded city the next time the region loads. Not while the game has that region loaded.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name. |
| `city` | string | required | the city's name or file name. |

## remove_region

*destructive*

Take a whole region away: its folder is moved into SiMCP's backups (not deleted). Not while the game has it loaded; the game's region list drops it at the next start.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name. |

## rename_region

*set*

Give a region a new name (shown in the game; the folder keeps its name). Not while the game has it loaded.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name. |
| `new_name` | string | required | the new name (1-32 letters, digits, spaces, - ' _). |

## set_region_layout

*act*

Give a region a new grid of city tiles (its config.bmp): width x height grid squares (1 km each) filled with small (1x1), medium (2x2) or large (4x4) city tiles. Refused when the region has founded cities. Reopens the region when the region view shows it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name (list_regions). |
| `width` | integer | required | grid squares east-west (1-64; a multiple of the tile's span). |
| `height` | integer | required | grid squares north-south. |
| `tile` | string | `'small'` | small, medium or large. |

## import_region_terrain

*destructive*

Shape a whole region from a height map, through the game's own region import (RegionBitmapLoad): every city tile of the region is deleted and generated again from its part of the map, then saved (about 13 s per small tile). Heights are metres: sea level is 250, the game stores grey x 3 m (0-765). The region view must show the region (load_region). A region with founded cities is refused unless replace_cities.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | required | the region's folder name (the one the region view shows). |
| `heights` | array of array of number or null | `null` | rows of heights in metres (north row first, west to east), any size from 2 x 2: resampled to the region's map size. Use this or image_path. |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | a greyscale image file (any common format) used instead: grey level x 3 m. |
| `replace_cities` | boolean | `false` | allow deleting founded cities. |
| `max_seconds` | number | `1800.0` | how long to wait for the game to generate the tiles. |

## load_region

*act*

Open a region in the region view (the game's own LoadRegion). Works from the region view; leave a city first.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the region's folder name as list_regions shows it (e.g. "MCP Test", "Timbuktu"). |

## load_city

*act*

Open a city of the loaded region with the region view's own LoadCity: with a name, the founded city of that name; without one, the first unfounded tile of the given size (it opens in god mode: terrain only). Returns the city's status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `''` | a founded city's name as list_regions shows it, or "" for an unfounded tile. |
| `size` | string | `'any'` | for an unfounded tile: "small" (64x64 cells), "medium" (128x128), "large" (256x256) or "any". |

## found_city

*act*

Found (establish) the unfounded tile that is open, as the player does: the Mayor Mode button, then the Establish City dialog with the city's and the mayor's names and the difficulty. After this the god-mode terrain tools are no longer available and the difficulty cannot change (the game's own rule).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the city's name (1-31 characters). |
| `mayor` | string | required | the mayor's name (1-31 characters). |
| `difficulty` | string | `'easy'` | "easy", "medium" or "hard" (sets the starting funds and the economy's difficulty). |

## set_speed

*set*

The game's speed buttons: "slow", "medium" or "fast" (like the buttons, this also un-pauses).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | string | required | "slow", "medium" or "fast". |

## set_paused

*set*

Pause or resume the simulation with the game's pause button.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paused` | boolean | required | true to pause, false to run. |

## game_options

*read*

The game's options: the Play Options dialog's switches (auto go to disaster, edge scrolling, expanded tooltips, urgent advice dialogs, auto edge reconciliation), sound and music, graphics settings and resolution, pause on focus loss. Read from the game's preferences.

No parameters.

## set_play_option

*set*

Switch one of the Play Options, as the dialog's Accept does (the game is told and saves its preferences in SiMCP's own user folder).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | string | required | auto_go_to_disaster, edge_scrolling, expanded_tooltips, urgent_advice_dialogs or auto_edge_reconciliation. |
| `on` | boolean | required | true to switch it on. |

## graphics_options

*set*

The Graphic Options dialog: with no arguments, read its settings; with arguments, set them as the player does (the game's own dialog: SiMCP clicks its buttons and presses Accept, and the game applies and saves them). Resolution, colour quality and renderer are reported only: SiMCP's game_launch sets the window.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visual_effects` | string | `''` | low, medium or high (also cars_and_sims, shadows, building_draw_speed, texture_quality, city_detail). |
| `cars_and_sims` | string | `''` | low, medium or high. |
| `shadows` | string | `''` | low, medium or high. |
| `building_draw_speed` | string | `''` | low, medium or high. |
| `texture_quality` | string | `''` | low, medium or high. |
| `city_detail` | string | `''` | low, medium or high. |
| `clouds_and_fog` | boolean or null | `null` | on or off (also waves, ui_translucency, color_cursor, variable_speed_automata). |
| `waves` | boolean or null | `null` | on or off. |
| `ui_translucency` | boolean or null | `null` | on or off. |
| `color_cursor` | boolean or null | `null` | on or off. |
| `variable_speed_automata` | boolean or null | `null` | on or off. |

## audio_options

*set*

The Audio Options dialog: with no arguments, read it; with arguments, set them through the game's own dialog (its checkboxes and volume sliders, then Accept; the game applies and saves them).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `music` | boolean or null | `null` | music on or off. |
| `music_volume` | integer or null | `null` | 0-100. |
| `sound` | boolean or null | `null` | sound effects on or off. |
| `sound_volume` | integer or null | `null` | 0-100. |
| `custom_tunes` | boolean or null | `null` | play the music in the game's custom music folder (only when it has some). |

## save_city

*destructive*

Save the open city with the game's own save, into its file in SiMCP's user folder (replacing the previous save). SiMCP's copies of the cities shipped with the game are kept as shipped unless allow_shipped.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_shipped` | boolean | `false` | also save over SiMCP's copy of a city that came with the game. |

## dialog_status

*read*

The game's open dialog windows, topmost first: title, texts and buttons (labels and ids). When a dialog is open the game waits for an answer; close_dialog answers it.

No parameters.

## close_dialog

*act*

Answer the topmost dialog by pressing one of its buttons, as the player clicks it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `button` | string | required | the button's label as dialog_status shows it (case-insensitive; a unique part is enough) or its id. |

## set_popups

*set*

Whether the game opens popup windows (advisor messages, message boxes) during play. With popups off the game keeps running unattended; advice still reaches the advisors panel and news (read them with advisors()).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | required | true = the game's normal popups, false = none. |

## leave_city

*destructive*

Go back to the region view without saving (unsaved changes to the city are lost).

No parameters.

## advance_time

*act*

Advance the open city by this many game days and pause exactly on the target day.

mode "natural" (default) lets the game play at its fast speed - everything happens as for a player who presses fast and waits (buildings finish construction, cars drive, idle work runs), about 10-20 days per second. "unthrottled" removes the game's spacing between days (much faster, but buildings finish on wall-clock time in this game, so fewer complete per day). "exact" steps days with the game's day code under a hidden pause (fastest and fully deterministic per day; construction barely progresses - use it for budget / time checks). The player's speed and pause state are restored. If max_seconds runs out first, remaining_days says how many days are left.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | `1` | game days to advance (1 or more). |
| `mode` | string | `'natural'` | natural, unthrottled or exact. |
| `max_seconds` | number | `90.0` | wall-clock limit for this call (keep it under your client's tool timeout). |

## city_status

*read*

The open city: name, mayor, founded or not, difficulty, size in cells, the game date, speed and pause state, read from the game's memory; and how many cheats SiMCP has used in it (cheat log).

No parameters.

## map_data

*read*

One data layer of the open city as a grid, read from the game's memory: the values the game's data views and simulation use. Call with no layer to list the layers. Values are per tract (tract_size cells square; rows[z][x] in tract units); a cell (x, z) is in tract (x // tract_size, z // tract_size).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | `''` | a layer name ("zones", "land_value", "crime", "police_coverage", "fire_coverage", "air_pollution", "water_pollution", "garbage", "power", "water", "traffic_congestion", "traffic_volume", "mayor_rating", ...); "" lists them. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | first cell column of the area to return (0 = west edge). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | first cell row of the area to return. |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | last cell column (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | last cell row (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |

## tile_info

*read*

Everything about one cell of the open city: the value of every data layer there, the terrain altitude at its corners, water depth and sea level, and the lot / building standing on it. Read from memory.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | cell column (0 = west edge). |
| `z` | integer | required | cell row (0 = north edge). |

## network_map

*read*

Where the roads, rails, highways, streets, power lines, pipes and subways are: a character map of the area (one string per cell row, rows[z - z0][x - x0]) with each cell's connected sides, read from the game's network pieces. Also lists pieces that connect to a neighbour city across the map edge, and - for areas of at most 400 cells - every piece with its sides per network.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | string | `''` | "" for everything above ground (pipes and subways are underground and share cells with roads), or one network: road, rail, elevated_highway, street, pipe, power_line, avenue, subway, light_rail, monorail, one_way_road, dirt_road, ground_highway. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | first cell column (0 = west edge). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | first cell row (0 = north edge). |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | last cell column (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | last cell row (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `traffic` | boolean | `false` | also list the busiest cells of the area with their trips per travel type. |

## neighbor_deals

*read*

The city's deals with neighbour cities (selling or buying power and water, exporting or importing garbage): partner tile, amount per month, the month's income or expense, state, dates; the month's deal totals; and the connections to neighbours (power lines, pipes, roads, rails... reaching the map edge).

No parameters.

## open_neighbor_deals

*act*

Open the Budget window's Neighbor Deals panel, as the player does after the advisor reports a possible deal: the game proposes every deal the connections and both cities' surplus and need allow, and those deals start at once (the panel has no accept step). A deal needs a connection: a power line, pipe or road to the map edge built with build_network(connect_neighbor=true).

No parameters.

## cancel_neighbor_deal

*act*

Cancel a running neighbour deal, as its "Cancel Deal" button does (the money stops at once; opening the panel again proposes it anew if it is still possible).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer | required | the deal's index from neighbor_deals. |

## find_route

*read*

The shortest way along connected network pieces from one cell to another (cells in order, plus the corner cells where the way turns) - for planning drives, checking that places are connected, or laying pipes.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | start cell column (must hold a piece of the network). |
| `z0` | integer | required | start cell row. |
| `x1` | integer | required | goal cell column. |
| `z1` | integer | required | goal cell row. |
| `kind` | string | `'car'` | "car" (roads, streets, avenues, one-way and dirt roads, highways) or one network name. |

## get_budget

*read*

The city's money: funds, the tax rate of every zone and wealth group, this month's income and expenses, last month's, year to date, the game's end-of-year estimate, and loans. Read from the game.

No parameters.

## set_tax

*set*

Set the tax rate of one zone and wealth group, as the Budget window's spinners do (0.0 to 20.0 percent in steps of 0.1; outside values are clamped). Returns the rate the game now uses.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | string | required | one of residential_low, residential_medium, residential_high, commercial_services_low, commercial_services_medium, commercial_services_high, commercial_office_medium, commercial_office_high, industrial_agriculture, industrial_dirty, industrial_manufacturing, industrial_high_tech. |
| `rate` | number | required | the tax rate in percent. |

## departments

*read*

The city's budget departments (police, fire, health, education, transit, utilities...): funding percentage, the most the player may set, and this month's expense and income for each.

No parameters.

## set_department_funding

*set*

Set a department's funding, as the Budget window's slider does (0 up to the department's maximum, usually 120 percent; clamped). It sets every building of the department to that funding (building_funding shows what that does to each one's service). Returns the new monthly expense.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `department` | string | required | the department's name as departments() lists it (e.g. "Police Dept.", "Education"; a unique part of the name is enough) or its id. |
| `percent` | number | required | the funding in percent of the full cost. |

## building_funding

*read*

A civic building's or power plant's funding and what it buys: each budget item (funding percent, full and current monthly cost), the game's response curve from funding to effect with the effect now, and the service measured in the game - power plant efficiency, condition and output capacity; police / fire station efficiency; school / hospital capacity, staff and enrolment. Funding below 100 percent saves money and weakens the service by the curve (fire stations and power plants lose effect faster than the money saved; school buses and ambulances keep half their coverage at zero).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | a cell of the building (column). |
| `z` | integer | required | a cell of the building (row). |

## strikes_and_jails

*read*

Whether police, firefighters, teachers or doctors are on strike and the chance of a strike now (from each station's funding through the game's strike curve - plugins may switch strikes off, as this setup does for the police), and the jails: capacity, inmates, criminals at large, arrests.

No parameters.

## set_building_funding

*set*

Set one building's funding, as its funding slider in the Budget window does (0 up to the item's maximum, usually 120 percent; clamped). Returns the cost and the measured service before and after.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | a cell of the building (column). |
| `z` | integer | required | a cell of the building (row). |
| `item` | string | required | power, police, fire, school_staff, school_buses, hospital_staff or ambulances (building_funding lists a building's items). |
| `percent` | number | required | the funding in percent of the full cost. |

## ordinances

*read*

Every ordinance the game knows (including those added by plugins): whether it is available to this city, enacted, its enactment and repeal fees, its current monthly income or cost, and its description.

No parameters.

## set_ordinance

*set*

Enact or repeal an ordinance, as the Ordinances panel does (only ordinances available to the city). Fees and monthly effects are settled with the month's budget.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the ordinance's name as ordinances() lists it (a unique part of the name is enough) or its id. |
| `enacted` | boolean | required | true to enact, false to repeal. |

## loans

*read*

The city's loans (principal, monthly payment, what is left to pay, when they end) and the bank's limits.

No parameters.

## take_loan

*act*

Take a loan from the bank, as the Loans window does: 5,000 to 100,000 in steps of 5,000, within the game's limits (number of loans and total borrowing). The money is added to the funds at once; it is repaid monthly with interest (SimCity 4 has no early repayment).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer | required | the loan amount. |

## demand

*read*

Residential, commercial and industrial demand per wealth group, as the game's demand graph shows it, with the share blocked by caps, plus the number of residents.

No parameters.

## lots

*read*

The lots of the open city with their building: position, size, facing, zone, wealth, state (occupied, abandoned, under construction...), historical, power, the building's name and exemplar id, and optionally how full each one is (residents or jobs against capacity, per wealth group).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string | `''` | only lots of this zone (e.g. "residential_low", "industrial_high", "plopped"); "" = all. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | west edge of the area (cells). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | north edge of the area (cells). |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | east edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | south edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `limit` | integer | `500` | at most this many lots in the answer (count always gives the total). |
| `occupancy` | boolean | `false` | add residents / jobs and capacity per lot (a few game calls per lot). |

## rename_city

*set*

Rename the open city and / or its mayor, as the city name window of the control panel does. The next save_city writes the city under its new name.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `''` | the city's new name (1-31 characters; "" = keep). |
| `mayor` | string | `''` | the mayor's new name ("" = keep). |

## make_historical

*act*

Make a zoned building historical (or not), as the "Make Historical" button of its query window does: the game will not redevelop or replace it (it can still be abandoned or bulldozed). Free.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | a cell of the building's lot (column). |
| `z` | integer | required | a cell of the building's lot (row). |
| `historical` | boolean | `true` | true to protect it, false to lift the protection. |

## advisors

*read*

What the city's advisors say now: each advisor's mood and current messages (title, mood, priority, text) - the same advice the game shows in its advisor panel, popups and news ticker.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_fluff` | boolean | `false` | also list the fluffy news (jokes without game meaning). |

## build_menu

*read*

What the player can plop now, from the game's build menus (with plugins): each item's name, lot and building ids, menus, size in cells, plop cost, monthly cost, and whether the menu offers it (available=false: greyed - a locked reward, a population or era requirement, an exclusion). menu="trees" lists the trees.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menu` | string | `''` | one menu only: parks, rail, transit (bus, subway, tram, parking, toll), ferries, power, water, garbage, police, jail, fire, education, health, airports, landmarks, rewards, or trees. "" = all. |

## plop

*act*

Plop a building from the build menus, as the player's plop tool does: the game's placement rules apply and its plop cost is charged. Refused when the menu greys it out (locked reward, requirement not met) or the spot is taken, too steep or under water (nothing is charged then).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `building` | string | required | a name from build_menu ("Coal Power Plant") or its lot or building id ("0x02000002"). |
| `x` | integer | required | west edge of the lot (cell). |
| `z` | integer | required | north edge of the lot (cell). |
| `facing` | string | `'north'` | the side the lot's front faces: north (toward smaller z), east, south or west. |

## build_network

*act*

Build a road, rail, pipe, power line or other network through cells, as the player drags it: one drag per leg between consecutive points, laid by the game's own path solver (diagonals and curves as the game makes them), each leg's cost charged to the funds (a leg the city cannot pay is not built).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | string | required | road, street, avenue, one_way_road, rail, light_rail, monorail, subway, elevated_highway, ground_highway, dirt_road, pipe or power_line. |
| `points` | array of array of integer | required | cells [[x, z], ...]: where the drag starts and each point where it bends or ends (2 to 64). To join an existing road, start or end ON one of its cells (a drag beside it does not connect). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report each leg's cost and whether the game allows it. |
| `connect_neighbor` | boolean | `false` | at the city edge, accept the game's offer to connect to the neighbour city. |
| `bridge` | string | `''` | over water, which bridge to build: a name from the leg's bridge_choices (or part of it, e.g. "Stone Arch") or its number; "" = the first. build_it=false lists the bridges offered. |

## zone

*act*

Zone (or de-zone) a rectangle of cells, as the player's zone tool does: the game's zoning rules (slope, size) and its cost per cell, charged to the funds. Areas larger than one drag (32 x 32, 48 x 48 for agriculture) are zoned in several drags.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone_type` | string | required | residential_low, residential_medium, residential_high, commercial_low, commercial_medium, commercial_high, agriculture, industrial_medium, industrial_high, military, airport, seaport, spaceport, landfill, or dezone. |
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |
| `streets` | boolean | `true` | lay the automatic streets inside large zones (false = the Ctrl-drag). |
| `alternate` | boolean | `false` | the Alt-drag variant of the zone tool. |

## bulldoze

*destructive*

Bulldoze everything on a rectangle of cells (buildings, lots, networks, trees), as the player's bulldozer does: the game's demolition cost is taken from the funds (as in the game, this can go below zero).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |

## plant_trees

*act*

Plant one tree in each cell of a rectangle, as the player's flora tool does: each tree's price is charged, and planting stops when the city cannot pay.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree` | string | required | a tree from build_menu(menu="trees"): its name ("Oak Tree") or id. |
| `x0` | integer | required | west edge (cell). |
| `z0` | integer | required | north edge (cell). |
| `x1` | integer | required | east edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `z1` | integer | required | south edge (cell, inclusive). |
| `build_it` | boolean | `true` | false = only report the cost. |

## graphs

*read*

The game's Graphs window: every graph (mayor rating, funds, income and expenses, population by type and age, demand, power, water, pollution, garbage, commute time, traffic volume, crime, education, life expectancy...) with each line's latest value in the units the window shows. graph_data gives the history of a line.

No parameters.

## graph_data

*read*

The history of one or more series the city keeps (the data behind the Graphs window and the advisors' trends): dated samples, oldest first. Most series get one sample a month; tax rates one a day.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | string | `''` | a graph title ("Funds (000s)", "Crime"), a line ("Power: Capacity"), a series name ("funds", "air_pollution", "tax_rate_residential_low") or an id ("0x4A5BA3D0"). "" lists every series kept. |
| `last` | integer | `24` | the newest this many samples per series (0 = all kept). |

## camera

*read*

Where the city view looks: the centre cell (x, z), the ground altitude there, zoom (1 far .. 6 close), rotation (0..3) and the viewport size in pixels.

No parameters.

## set_camera

*set*

Move the city view as the player does (the game's own view commands); omitted values stay as they are.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, west-east (-1 = keep). |
| `z` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, north-south (-1 = keep). |
| `zoom` | integer | `0` | 1 (far) to 6 (close); 0 = keep. |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3 (each step is a quarter turn clockwise); -1 = keep. |

## day_night

*set*

The day/night cycle, as god mode's button sets it: day_and_night (the clock runs), day (always day) or night (always night). With no mode it reads the setting.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `''` | day_and_night, day, night, or "" to read. |

## snapshot

*observe*

A picture of the city as the game draws it (the game's own snapshot of its view, with its UI), after moving the view if asked. Returns the camera and the image; the full-size PNG is kept in SiMCP's snapshots folder.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, west-east (-1 = keep). |
| `z` | integer | `-1` | centre cell, north-south (-1 = keep). |
| `zoom` | integer | `0` | 1 (far) to 6 (close); 0 = keep. |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3; -1 = keep. |
| `width` | integer | `1024` | scale the image to this many pixels wide (the PNG keeps the full size). |

## disaster_status

*read*

Disasters going on in the open city (fires, volcanoes, earthquakes, riots, toxic spills...) with their locations, and the god-mode Disasters menu.

No parameters.

## start_disaster

*act*

Start a disaster from the god-mode Disasters menu at a cell, with the game's own disaster tool (as the player's click). Disasters unfold while the game runs: set_paused(false) or advance_time afterwards.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disaster` | string | required | volcano, earthquake, fire, meteor, tornado, lightning, robot_attack, autosaurus_wrecks or ufo. |
| `x` | integer | required | cell, west-east. |
| `z` | integer | required | cell, north-south. |

## dispatch

*act*

Send emergency units to a cell with the game's dispatch tools (as the player's dispatch buttons): the city needs a station of that kind with a free unit and a road route to the cell.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | string | required | fire, police, fire_plane or police_helicopter. |
| `x` | integer | required | cell, west-east. |
| `z` | integer | required | cell, north-south. |

## cheat

*act*

Run one of the game's player cheats - outside honest play, so every use is logged (SiMCP's cheats.jsonl) and counted in city_status. Only vetted cheats run, with checked arguments: weaknesspays (+1,000), riskymoney (+10,000, may start a riot), howdryiam (all watered), fightthepower (all powered), barstuck, whattimeizit <hour>, stopwatch pause|resume|magnify <n>, showtime, whererufrom <city name>, hellomynameis <mayor name>, dollyllama, casper [off], gp on|off. Developer and crashing cheats are refused.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the cheat (case-insensitive). |
| `argument` | string | `''` | its argument, if it takes one (a single word for names). |

## city_figures

*read*

The city figures the game computes for its advisors (about 190 game.g_* values: population per zone and wealth, tile and building counts, coverage, congestion, funds, borrowing...), read from the game's own Lua state. With no expression it lists the names; with one it evaluates it, read-only.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | string | `''` | e.g. "game.g_population", "game.g_road_tile_count + game.g_street_tile_count", "game.trend_value(game_trends.G_FUNDS, 12)". Allowed: game.g_* values, read-only game functions (trend_value, trend_slope, trend_count, ordinance_is_on, difficulty_level...), the constant tables (game_trends, tuning_constants...), numbers, strings, arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, tostring, tonumber, math.*. |

## missions

*read*

U-Drive-It: the missions the City Situations advisor offers now, and the current mission and vehicle (status, time used and limit, target cell and distance, vehicle cell and heading).

No parameters.

## start_mission

*act*

Ask the game to offer a U-Drive-It mission (by its title or guid from missions()). The game picks a vehicle of that kind out in the city and opens the offer dialog: answer it with close_dialog("Accept"), close_dialog("Free Drive") or close_dialog("Cancel"). The city must have been running for a few seconds so vehicles are out.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mission` | string | required | the mission title or guid. |

## drive

*act*

Hold driving keys for a while, as the player does, then release them; returns the mission and vehicle state. The game must be running (not paused). Heading x is east, z south; "left" turns toward the vehicle's left.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` | array of string | required | any of accelerate, brake, left, right, special (horn / siren / hose), alternate, off_road, climb, dive, power_up, power_down - held together. |
| `seconds` | number | `1.0` | how long to hold them (0 to 10). |

## stop_driving

*act*

Leave the vehicle (the Escape key), ending a free drive or giving up a mission.

No parameters.

## my_sims

*read*

The five My Sim slots: for each Sim living in the city, name, age, sign, wealth, home, job and where it is now (cell).

No parameters.

## move_in_sim

*act*

Make a My Sim and move it into the house on a cell, through the game's My Sims panel, its Select A My Sim dialog and the move-in tool. The face sets the gender (and a preset name and sign, which name and sign override). The game then reports through the Sim's own advice balloons.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | a cell of the house (west-east). |
| `z` | integer | required | a cell of the house (north-south). |
| `face` | string | `''` | one of the dialog's faces - the game's 21 or one's own (design_my_sim_face) - by number or preset name (my_sim_faces lists them); "" = the default. |
| `name` | string | `''` | the Sim's name (1-31 characters; "" = the face's preset name). |
| `sign` | string | `''` | capricorn, aquarius, pisces, aries, taurus, gemini, cancer, leo, virgo, libra, scorpio or sagittarius ("" = the face's). |

## my_sim_faces

*read*

The faces the Select A My Sim dialog offers: number, preset name, sign and gender (the game's 21, then faces of one's own).

No parameters.

## design_my_sim_face

*act*

Add a face of one's own to the Select A My Sim dialog (as the game's "import from The Sims" does): a 36 x 36 picture in the MySim folder of SiMCP's user folder and its entry (name, gender, sign) in MySims.dat. The dialog reads them each time it opens; move_in_sim(x, z, face=name) then moves a Sim with it in.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the face's preset name (1-31 characters; not one of the game's faces). The same name replaces it. |
| `gender` | string | `'male'` | male or female. |
| `sign` | string | `'aries'` | capricorn, aquarius, pisces, aries, taurus, gemini, cancer, leo, virgo, libra, scorpio or sagittarius. |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | a photo or picture (cropped to its centre square, scaled to 36 x 36); "" draws a simple face. |
| `skin_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the drawn face's skin colour. |
| `hair_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the drawn face's hair colour. |
| `shirt_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the drawn face's shirt colour. |

## remove_my_sim_face

*destructive*

Take a face of one's own out of the Select A My Sim dialog; its picture moves to SiMCP's backups. Sims already living with it show a blank face until the picture is back in the MySim folder.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the face's preset name (my_sim_faces). |

## terrain_brushes

*read*

The terrain brushes available now: in a founded city the mayor's raise / lower / level (charged); before founding, god mode's brushes (mountains, valleys, canyons, craters, lakes, levelling, smoothing, erosion, plains... free).

No parameters.

## terraform

*act*

Hold a terrain brush on cells, as the player holds the mouse: the effect grows with the time held; with several cells the brush moves along them. In mayor mode each application is charged. Returns the altitudes before and after and the cost.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brush` | string | required | a name from terrain_brushes() (mayor mode: raise, lower, level). |
| `cells` | array of array of integer | required | [[x, z], ...] - one cell, or a path for the brush to move along. |
| `seconds` | number | `1.0` | how long to hold (0.1 to 10). |

## content_designs

*read*

The buildings SiMCP designed (its plugin files in SiMCP's own Plugins folder): name, ids, file, state.

No parameters.

## design_building

*act*

Design a new building for the build menus from one of the game's own menu items (its models, props and textures) under a new name, description and costs; it is written as a plugin file into SiMCP's own Plugins folder. The game loads plugins at start-up: quit_game and game_launch, then it is in build_menu like any other.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the new building's name, shown in the menu. |
| `template` | string | required | a Maxis item from build_menu: its name ("Playground") or lot id. |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu description. |
| `plop_cost` | integer | `-1` | the plop cost (-1 = the template's). |
| `monthly_cost` | integer | `-1` | the monthly cost (-1 = the template's). |
| `bulldoze_cost` | integer | `-1` | the bulldoze cost (-1 = the template's). |

## design_model_building

*act*

Design a new building with its own 3D model and textures (a block with a window grid and a flat roof) on its own paved lot, for the Parks menu; written as a plugin into SiMCP's own Plugins folder. The game loads plugins at start-up: quit_game and game_launch, then it is in build_menu like any other.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the new building's name, shown in the menu. |
| `width_m` | number | required | west-east size in metres (a cell is 16 m; it must fit the lot). |
| `depth_m` | number | required | north-south size in metres. |
| `height_m` | number | required | height in metres (2..400). |
| `wall_rgb` | array of integer | required | the wall colour [r, g, b] (0..255). |
| `roof_rgb` | array of integer | required | the roof colour [r, g, b]. |
| `windows` | boolean | `true` | draw a window on every 4 m x 4 m of wall. |
| `lot_cells` | integer | `1` | the lot's size in cells a side (1..6). |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu description. |
| `plop_cost` | integer | `500` | the plop cost. |
| `monthly_cost` | integer | `20` | the monthly cost. |
| `ground` | string | `'plaza'` | the lot's ground texture: paving, plaza, concrete, asphalt, grass, lawn, meadow, gravel, garden, sand or parking. |
| `objects` | array of object or null | `null` | things on the lot around the building, as for design_park: [{"prop": id or name, "x": m, "z": m, "rotation": 0-3}, {"tree": name, "x": m, "z": m}, {"ground": name, "x": m, "z": m}]. |
| `model_path` | string | `''` | your own 3D model instead of the block: a Wavefront OBJ (y up, +z facing the street, faces counter-clockwise seen from outside) with its MTL and PNG / JPEG textures (texture coordinates 0..1; the game does not repeat textures). Its size (times model_scale, in metres) replaces width, depth and height; the walls and roof colours are then unused. |
| `model_scale` | number | `1.0` | metres per model unit. |
| `department` | object or null | `null` | a budget department of its own for the building, in the Budget window: {"name": "Museum Fund", "group": "government" (or business_deals, city_beautification, health_education, public_safety, transportation, utilities), "monthly_cost": 40, "monthly_income": 0}; each building of the design adds its line. |

## design_tree

*act*

Design a new tree type for the game's tree menu (planted with plant_trees or the player's tree tool): its own 3D model (three crossed planes) with a painted texture - broadleaf, conifer or palm in the colours given - or a picture you supply. Written as a plugin into SiMCP's own Plugins folder; the game loads it at start-up (quit_game, game_launch). Returns the design and its texture.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the tree's name, shown in the menu. |
| `shape` | string | `'broadleaf'` | broadleaf, conifer or palm (ignored with image_path). |
| `height_m` | number | `12.0` | height in metres (2..40). |
| `width_m` | number | `8.0` | crown width in metres (1..16; a cell is 16 m). |
| `leaf_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the foliage colour [r, g, b] (default green). |
| `trunk_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the trunk colour [r, g, b] (default brown). |
| `cost` | integer | `3` | the price of each tree planted (0..10000; the game's trees cost 3). |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu description. |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | a PNG of the tree on a transparent background, used as the texture instead of painting one. |

## design_car

*act*

Design a new car for the city's traffic: its own 3D model (a sedan, van or pickup body with a painted texture, head and tail lights, the game's shadow and night lights), driven by the commuters of one wealth class. Written as a plugin into SiMCP's own Plugins folder; the game loads it at start-up (quit_game, game_launch). Returns the design and its texture.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the car's name (shown when a car is queried). |
| `kind` | string | `'sedan'` | sedan, van or pickup. |
| `body_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the paint colour [r, g, b] (default blue). |
| `wealth` | string | `'cheap'` | who drives it: cheap, middle or rich (the game's three commuter car classes). |

## game_props

*read*

The props that can stand on a lot (benches, fountains, signs, lamps, statues... the game's 1,544 and SiMCP's own prop designs), found by name - for design_park and design_model_building objects.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | `''` | part of the name ("bench", "fountain", "lamp"); "" lists the first ones. |
| `limit` | integer | `40` | how many to return. |

## design_prop

*act*

Design a new prop - a box, cylinder, cone or sign (a board on a post; image_path puts a picture on its street side) in one colour - to place on lots with design_park or design_model_building. Written as a plugin; the game loads it at start-up. Returns the design and its texture.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the prop's name. |
| `shape` | string | `'box'` | box, cylinder, cone or sign. |
| `width_m` | number | `2.0` | west-east size in metres (0.2..32). |
| `depth_m` | number | `2.0` | north-south size in metres (0.2..32; a sign's board is 0.3 m thick). |
| `height_m` | number | `2.0` | height in metres (0.2..60). |
| `rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the colour [r, g, b] (default grey). |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | a picture for the sign's face (any common format). |
| `model_path` | string | `''` | your own 3D model (Wavefront OBJ with MTL and textures, as for design_model_building) instead of a shape; its size times model_scale replaces width, depth and height. |
| `model_scale` | number | `1.0` | metres per model unit. |
| `animation` | string | `''` | spin (turns about its vertical axis) or sway (rocks gently), as the game's animated props. |
| `hours` | array of number or null | `null` | [from, to]: shown only at these hours of the game's day (may wrap midnight: [19, 6] = at night). |
| `dates` | object or null | `null` | {"start": [month, day], "days": n, "every": 365}: shown only then (holiday decorations...). |

## design_seasonal_tree

*act*

Design a tree that follows the seasons, for lots (design_park / design_model_building objects {"seasonal_tree": name, ...}): spring blossom from 1 March, summer from 1 June, autumn colours from 1 September, bare branches (a broadleaf) or snow (a conifer) from 1 December. The game shows each season's picture on its dates. (Trees planted with plant_trees cannot change: the game runs no growth or succession for flora.)

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the tree's name. |
| `shape` | string | `'broadleaf'` | broadleaf, conifer or palm (palms stay the same all year). |
| `height_m` | number | `12.0` | height in metres (2..40). |
| `width_m` | number | `8.0` | crown width in metres (1..16). |
| `leaf_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the summer foliage colour. |
| `trunk_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | the trunk colour. |

## design_park

*act*

Design a park (or plaza, garden, sculpture court...) for the Parks menu: a lot laid out with the game's props, SiMCP's prop designs, trees and ground textures. Positions are metres from the lot's north-west corner; the street runs along the lot's south (+z) edge. Written as a plugin; the game loads it at start-up.

| parameter | type | default | description |

| `name` | string | required | the park's name, shown in the menu. |
| `objects` | array of object | required | what stands on it: [{"prop": id or name, "x": m, "z": m, "rotation": 0-3}, {"tree": name or id, "x": m, "z": m}, {"seasonal_tree": name, "x": m, "z": m}, {"ground": texture name, "x": m, "z": m} (that cell's ground)]. |
| `lot_cells` | integer | `1` | the lot's size in cells a side (1..6; a cell is 16 m). |
| `ground` | string | `'grass'` | the ground texture of every cell: paving, plaza, concrete, asphalt, grass, lawn, meadow, gravel, garden, sand or parking. |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu description. |
| `plop_cost` | integer | `200` | the plop cost. |
| `monthly_cost` | integer | `10` | the monthly cost. |

| `model_scale` | number | `1.0` | metres per model unit. |

## design_ordinance

*act*

Design a new ordinance for the Ordinances window (through the installed custom ordinance DLL): its monthly income or cost, enactment cost, effects and when it becomes available. Once a city is saved with it, the game keeps the ordinance as it was then.

|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the ordinance's name. |

| `condition` | string | `''` | when it becomes available: a read-only expression like an advice trigger ("game.g_city_r_population > 2000"); empty = always. |

*act*

Design a new god-mode terrain brush: one of the game's brushes (terrain_brushes in god mode lists them: mountain_default, valley_lake, plains, canyon, crater, smoothing...) with a wider or narrower reach and a stronger or gentler effect. Written as a plugin; after a restart, terraform(brush="simcp_<name>") uses it before a city is founded.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the brush's name. |
| `base` | string | `'mountain_default'` | the game brush it starts from. |

## puzzle_pieces

*read*

The puzzle pieces the network tool can place whole (the game's interchanges and ramps, and NAM's thousands of pieces: roundabouts, turn lanes, overpasses, transitions...), from the game's own RUL0 rules, named from the RUL0 text NAM ships. Without arguments: the count and the groups.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | `''` | words in the piece's name (e.g. "roundabout", "cloverleaf", "turn lane"). |
| `group` | string | `''` | a group (NAM's RUL0 part, e.g. "AvenueRoundabouts", "Clovers"). |
| `hid` | string | `''` | one piece's id (hex): its size, cells, handle, rotations (Home / End) and Tab ring. |
| `limit` | integer | `40` | how many to list. |

## place_puzzle_piece

*act*

Place a puzzle piece as the game's puzzle-piece tool does: its handle on cell (x, z) (the cell under the pointer), the piece's own networks laid and its cost charged to the city. Pieces that join networks need them there (e.g. a single-tile roundabout on a road crossing); others stand alone.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hid` | string | required | the piece's id (puzzle_pieces finds them); its other rotations are other ids (puzzle_pieces(hid=...)). |
| `x` | integer | required | the handle's cell, west-east. |
| `z` | integer | required | the handle's cell, north-south. |
| `build` | boolean | `true` | false only checks that it fits and reports the cost. |
| `auto_fit` | boolean | `false` | also try the four neighbouring cells and the piece's other rotations, as the tool does while the player moves the pointer. |

## design_puzzle_piece

*act*

Make a new puzzle piece from ground networks laid in the open city (build_network them first, as a template): every network cell of the rectangle becomes part of the piece, its tiles copied as they look now and their traffic paths with them. open_ends lays the cells whose networks leave the rectangle as ordinary network, so other networks can join the piece there (a placed piece's own tiles cannot be built over). The piece joins the game when SiMCP next starts it (quit_game, game_launch); place_puzzle_piece(hid, x, z) then puts its north-west cell on (x, z), in four rotations. Keep a piece while saved cities use it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the piece's name (puzzle_pieces(group="SiMCP") lists SiMCP's pieces). |
| `x0` | integer | required | the rectangle's west cell. |
| `z0` | integer | required | its north cell. |
| `x1` | integer | required | its east cell (at most 16 cells across). |
| `z1` | integer | required | its south cell. |
| `cost` | integer | `-1` | what placing it costs (-1: 10 per cell). |
| `open_ends` | boolean | `true` | lay the ends as ordinary network (true), or keep every cell fixed (false). |

*read*

The bridges the game loads (its own, NAM's and other plugins'), with the name the bridge chooser shows. Which of them a drag can use depends on the network and the crossing: build_network(..., build_it=false) lists the ones offered there.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | `''` | words in the name. |

## design_bridge

*act*

A new bridge: a copy of one the game offers (its pieces and look) under a new name, optionally with its deck at another height above the water. It joins the game's bridge lists when SiMCP next starts the game (quit_game, game_launch); then build_network(..., bridge=name) builds it wherever its base would fit.

| parameter | type | default | description |

| `name` | string | required | the bridge's name, as the bridge chooser will show it. |
| `base` | string | required | the bridge it copies (a name from bridges() or a drag's bridge_choices, e.g. "Stone Arch"). |
| `height_m` | number | `-1.0` | the deck's height above the water in metres (0-200; -1 keeps the base's). |

## design_transit_station

*act*

A new transit station that works as the game's own of that kind: its lot is a copy of the game's station lot (its size, the network tiles of transit-enabled lots - light rail, monorail, toll booths, ferries -, its props and ground) and its building keeps the station's transit properties; SiMCP gives it its own model (a generated block, or an OBJ model) and name. It shows in the transit menu after a restart (quit_game, game_launch); plop places it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the station's name in the menu. |
| `kind` | string | required | bus, subway, light_rail, light_rail_subway, monorail, passenger_rail, freight_rail, car_ferry, passenger_ferry, parking or toll_booth. |
| `width_m` | number | `10.0` | the generated building's width (it must fit the station's lot). |
| `depth_m` | number | `10.0` | its depth. |
| `height_m` | number | `6.0` | its height. |
| `wall_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | its wall colour. |
| `roof_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | its roof colour. |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu text. |
| `plop_cost` | integer | `-1` | what placing it costs (-1: the game's station's). |
| `monthly_cost` | integer | `-1` | its monthly cost (-1: the game's station's). |
| `model_path` | string | `''` | an OBJ model to use instead of the block (its size replaces width / depth / height). |
| `model_scale` | number | `1.0` | metres per OBJ unit. |

## lot_layout

*read*

What a lot holds, object by object, as the Lot Editor shows it: each row's index, type (building, prop, ground, tree, network, water, land), what it is (id, name - a list of ids is a prop family, one picked at random), where (x, z in metres from the lot's north-west corner; the street is on the +z edge), its rotation and size. Reads the game's own lots and SiMCP's designs.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | string | required | a lot id (0x... from build_menu) or a menu item's name. |

## edit_lot

*act*

A new menu item from one of the game's lots edited as in the Lot Editor: rows removed, moved or turned, and props, trees and ground textures added (lot_layout gives the rows). The building and the rest stay as they are. The game loads it at the next start (quit_game, game_launch).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the new item's name. |
| `lot` | string | required | the game's lot to start from (a lot id from build_menu, or the item's name). |
| `remove` | array of integer or null | `null` | row indexes to take out (not the building's). |
| `move` | array of object or null | `null` | [{"index": n, "x": m, "z": m, "rotation": 0-3}] - rows to move or turn. |
| `add` | array of object or null | `null` | [{"prop": id or name, "x": m, "z": m, "rotation": 0-3}, {"tree": name, ...}, {"ground": texture, "x", "z"}] - as design_park's objects. |
| `description` | string | `''` | the menu text. |
| `plop_cost` | integer | `-1` | what placing it costs (-1: as the original). |
| `monthly_cost` | integer | `-1` | its monthly cost (-1: as the original). |

## terrain_look

*act*

The look of all terrain (global, every city): the game's own ground, beach and cliff textures recoloured, and its texture table moved drier or wetter, as one plugin. Plugins load at start, and the running game keeps it open: quit_game, set the look, then game_launch. Saved cities take the new look.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `look` | string | `''` | "" = the current look; default (the game's own), lush, arid, arctic, autumn, or custom (only the values below). |
| `moisture_shift` | integer or null | `null` | move the table's ground textures this many steps along sand -> grass -> dark grass (-7..7; + greener, - drier). |
| `saturation` | number or null | `null` | colour saturation (0..2, 1 = unchanged). |
| `brightness` | number or null | `null` | brightness (0.5..1.5). |
| `tint_rgb` | array of integer or null | `null` | a colour the textures' average moves towards (their pattern stays). |
| `tint_strength` | number or null | `null` | how far (0..1). |
| `snow` | number or null | `null` | snow cover (0..1; beach and cliffs take less). |
| `autumn` | number or null | `null` | turn green parts orange-brown (0..1). |

## design_advice

*act*

Write a new piece of advice or a news headline for the game's advisors, as a Lua plugin like the game's own advice scripts: the advisor shows it when its trigger is true. The game loads it at start-up (quit_game, game_launch); advisors() then lists it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | a name for the design (content_designs lists it). |
| `advisor` | string | required | utilities, health_education, city_planning, transportation, environment, finances, safety, or news (the news ticker). |
| `title` | string | required | the headline (plain text; <b>, <i> allowed; #city# becomes the city's name). |
| `message` | string | required | the advice text (plain text with <b>, <i>, <u>, <br>, <p>; no links). |
| `trigger` | string | `'1'` | when to show it - a read-only expression of the city's values, e.g. "game.g_city_r_population > 1000" or "game.g_funds < 5000"; "1" = at once. lua_query lists the values. |
| `mood` | string | `'neutral'` | alarm, bad, neutral, good or fluff. |
| `priority` | integer | `50` | 0-100 (higher shows first). |
| `once` | boolean | `true` | show it only the first time the trigger is true. |
| `news_only` | boolean | `false` | only in the news ticker, not as an advisor message. |
| `timeout_days` | integer | `30` | how long it stays. |

## design_growable_building

*act*

Design a building that grows by itself in zones (a house, shop, office or factory) with its own 3D model and lot. A game growable of the same purpose, wealth and lot size lends its zone types, demand, pollution and capacity; the design gets its own building family and carries all four building styles, so the city may grow it on fitting zoned lots when demand calls for it. Written as a plugin into SiMCP's own Plugins folder; the game loads it at start-up (quit_game, game_launch).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the building's name (shown in its query window). |
| `purpose` | string | required | residential, commercial_services, commercial_office, agriculture, industrial_processing, industrial_manufacturing or industrial_high_tech. |
| `wealth` | integer | required | 1 ($), 2 ($$) or 3 ($$$) (industry and agriculture have fewer kinds). |
| `width_m` | number | required | west-east size in metres (it must fit the lot: 16 m per cell). |
| `depth_m` | number | required | north-south size in metres. |
| `height_m` | number | required | height in metres (2..400). |
| `wall_rgb` | array of integer | required | wall colour [r, g, b]. |
| `roof_rgb` | array of integer | required | roof colour [r, g, b]. |
| `windows` | boolean | `true` | draw a window on every 4 m x 4 m of wall. |
| `lot_width` | integer | `1` | lot width in cells along the road (1..6). Lots one cell deep rarely develop; 2 deep is common. |
| `lot_depth` | integer | `2` | lot depth in cells (1..6). |
| `stage` | integer | `0` | growth stage (1 = the earliest; 0 = the template's). |
| `capacity` | integer | `0` | residents or jobs (0 = the template's). |
| `description` | string | `''` | a note kept in the design list. |

## disable_design

*destructive*

Take a SiMCP design out of the game: its file moves to SiMCP's content-disabled folder (nothing is deleted); restart the game for it to leave the menus. Buildings of it already in cities stay as they are.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the design's name. |

## quit_game

*destructive*

Quit SimCity 4 without saving (an open city's unsaved changes are lost; save first if needed).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | `false` | end the process instead of asking the game to quit (use only if the game no longer responds). |

## setup_check

*read*

What SiMCP needs on this machine, checked without starting the game: Windows, Python, the game's build, the SiMCP DLLs, SiMCP's home folder, your plugins (mirrored read-only) and NAM. Each check has ok and, when not ok, a hint.

No parameters.
